meaningMnemonic: This radical is the same as the kanji. It means above .
Do you see the big guy on top, holding spatulas and looming over a grill and open flames? That's why this is the charcoal radical. Without charcoal, this guy ain't grillin' nothin'.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means district .
There's a mysterious man in a fedora hat and a trench coat, smoking a cigarette and looking into the distance. What could this man possibly want, or what is he waiting for? How mysterious.
If you look at this radical right, you'll see a NOSE (with a squinty eye on the left).
Hey, it's that giant you learned before. But... but its arms are chained. They're chained because you caught the giant and now it's your servant !

A rice paddy you'd want to kiss is one that would probably have a cool abbreviation for their name, like Ri'-Pad. Yeah, that's definitely a cool abbreviation! Hints Try to imagine how cool and confident Ri'-Pad is, they probably grow and wear their rice in a cool and trendy way, like a middle part or something.
readingMnemonic: An abbreviation like Ri'-Pad is sure to get a strong reac tion ( りゃく ) — some will find it a little pretentious, some will hate it, but most will probably think it's really cool. Hints Try to visualize the different reactions people have to the name Ri'-Pad. What reaction did you have? What face did you make when you saw it?

meaningMnemonic: Grain s get blame d for how much they accumulate . If the grains accumulate too much then they make more work for the farmers. If they accumulate too little, then they're starving the people. Ugh, grains just can't win with you people. They're blamed for everything. Hints Picture a pile of grains accumulating in size while a person watches. No matter how large the pile gets, the person keeps blaming them for something!
readingMnemonic: Now the grains have accumulate d a ton, they're overflowing in their grain sacks, and the farmer freezes and says, "Now those are some sexy ( せき ) grains." Hints Is that why people become farmers? Because they think... accumulating a lot of grains is sexy? People are weird.

meaningMnemonic: There’s a tsunami in heaven and you take a small drop of water and append it to the tsunami. Now the tsunami is big enough to destroy all of heaven. The small drop that you appended to the tsunami was just enough to push it over the edge, reaching full destruction capability. Hints Take a small drop of water and append it to the tsunami. Feel the drop of water on your finger and visualize yourself flicking it at the tsunami as it races towards heaven.
readingMnemonic: Just after you append the small drop of water to the tsunami, it grows ten ( てん ) stories high. Before it was only nine, but since you appended that drop, the tsunami is now a full ten stories tall. Hints Look up at this ten story tall tsunami. It looks big and powerful. Feel the water spray from the tsunami as it towers over you.

meaningMnemonic: Under a roof , but still in the sun , a woman is laying out a fabulous banquet . The woman doesn't want anyone to burn from the sun, but banquets are best outside, so she's set up a roof to protect her and her guests. Hints Picture a large banquet of food on a sunny day, covered by an outdoor roof, and a woman carefully setting it all up.
readingMnemonic: Unfortunately, the banquet roof comes crashing down right before the guests arrive, and it end s ( えん ) before it can start. Hints Honestly though, have you ever been to a banquet that ended well? Something always goes wrong when you have that many people under one roof.

meaningMnemonic: If you're a tree anti (someone who's against trees), then you won't mind if I turn all of them into board s! Hahaha! Hints "Boards are much more useful than trees." – The Anti-Tree Association. Now picture this sign on a big machine that's cutting up all the trees into big boards.
readingMnemonic: The Tree Lovers Association has one word when they see you turning trees into board s: " Ban ned ( ばん )," they shout at you. "Boards mean you're banned!" Hints You couldn't care less about getting banned from the Tree Lovers Association. You and your Anti-Tree Association still keep on turning every tree into boards, ban or no ban. Damn those trees!

meaningMnemonic: In the dirt you place a cross and surround it with a net made of clothes to keep it safe, but this net tends to break . Of course it breaks, it's just some clothes you tied together. Hints Imagine what this janky makeshift net would look like. It's both comical and sad. Every day you set it up around the cross, but next morning it's lying in a broken heap in the dirt. What keeps breaking it?!
readingMnemonic: You realize what keeps making your net break are kay aks ( かい ). The cross and net are right next to a river trail that kayakers do their kayaking in, and every time they go by their paddles smack into your net and break it. Hints Imagine the rage you'd feel at these unrepentant kayakers who keep breaking your stuff. Oh, and don't forget to be angry at yourself — for putting the cross and net so close to a river that kayaks can't even go by without breaking it.

meaningMnemonic: A good leader will use charcoal to mark her colleague s. Sometimes if leaders aren't around all the time, people will get rebellious and act badly toward people who can get them in trouble. So when you mark them with charcoal you know that someone close with your leader is around and you should probably stop being a butt. Hints Imagine seeing one of the leader's colleagues walking around, watching you. You'd get back to work and stop goofing around, right?
readingMnemonic: You have to be good around her colleague s, because if you aren't your row ( りょう ) boat permit will be taken away. Row boating is the only fun you ever get to have, besides learning kanji. So act as best you can around the leader's colleagues so you don't lose your row boat rights. Hints Imagine goofing off in your row boat and then seeing one of the colleagues waiting on the shore for you. No! She's gonna take your row boat away!

meaningMnemonic: A tree is not a cup of liquid or a counter for cups . Don’t get them mixed up. The last time you tried making a cup out of a tree to count your throat got filled with splinters when you used it. There wasn't even any liquid in it. Hints Imagine cutting a tree into a cup of liquid and focus on the pain in your throat when you try to actually use it. Instead you kick the tree and angrily count cups of liquid in your head, because they simply are NOT the same.
readingMnemonic: Another way to remember the counter for cups using a cup of liquid would be by creating and memorizing a hai ku ( はい ) about them. Aren’t haikus useful? Hints Think of a haiku about a cup of liquid and a counter for cups. Use that haiku to help remember this kanji.

meaningMnemonic: A woman who is good is my daughter . My daughter is a good woman, I guarantee it. Hints Look at how good this woman is! She’s my daughter! She’s good! You wish your daughter was as good a woman as mine is!
readingMnemonic: Your daughter , on the other hand, is not a good woman. Your daughter looks like a moose who may ( むすめ ) not be able to find its way out of a wet paper bag. Your daughter looks like a moose who may lose its way without a map. Your daughter looks like a moose who may do lots of stupid things. Hints Think about how your daughter is basically a moose who may do dumb things. How ashamed you feel. How very, very ashamed. Unlike how I feel about my wonderful, perfect, not a moose-like daughter.

meaningMnemonic: They say to wear a hat to cover your hair if your doctor diagnose s you with hair loss. It's the best option, folks. Hints Imagine the doctor diagnosing you with hair loss. He pulls out a hat and places it on your poor, thinning hair.
readingMnemonic: You just had the doctor diagnose you with hair loss. How terrible! You stumble out of the room, dumbfounded. Not paying attention, you bang your shin ( しん ) on the table. Your shin really hurts. What an awful day. Hints Hold your shin as you feel the throbbing pain in it. Even though the pain is so extreme, you can’t help but still think about the diagnosis you got from the doctor.

meaningMnemonic: Above you on a small stool is the eye of the one who will direct and supervise you at work. He’s really high above you, so all you can see is the glint of his supervising eye. But you can hear him shouting directions clearly, telling you exactly what to do. Hints Look up and see that eye, shining down and supervising you closely. Hear the man shouting as he directs you in one task after another. It makes you uncomfortable, honestly.
readingMnemonic: A man who can direct others so well must be Toku gawa ( とく ) Ieyasu. Sure enough, when he finally comes down off his stool you see that he’s the ghost of Tokugawa Ieyasu!!! That explains why you could only make out the ghostly gleam of his supervising eye before. Hints Tokugawa lingers before you in full shogun garb, then nods his head in approval, winks, and disappears.

meaningMnemonic: Under this roof someone odd is trying to draw near to you. You back up, but they continue to draw near anyway. Hints Imagine being under the same roof as an odd person who's always trying to draw near to you. You don't want anything to do with them, but they won't back off.
readingMnemonic: They continue to draw near until you can't take it anymore. You run out from under the roof, slam the door closed, and lock it with a key ( き ). Hints You hold the key tightly in your hand and press your ear to the door. You can still hear the odd person drawing near. Hopefully this key keeps them away.

meaningMnemonic: In the morning , you use a gun on your nose to make it dry . Hints Don't worry, there aren't bullets in the gun. It's an air gun! So just imagine shooting the air into your nose every morning to make sure it's nice and dry.
readingMnemonic: This technique for a nice dry nose was invented by Genghis Khan ( かん )! Well, not him, but someone who worked under him. You see, he had a bit of a damp nose problem. Hints Now the next time you manage to get your nose nice and dry, think back to our founding father Genghis Khan and thank him for where you are today.

meaningMnemonic: A district that lack s things will be in Europe . Hints Picture a map of Europe in your mind. Now picture little words saying which district is lacking what. This one is lacking water. That one is lacking food.
readingMnemonic: Europe is lacking so much because their 王 ( おう ) keeps taking everything. Hints Okay, so maybe this is an old view of Europe. But back in the old days the 王 s there would take everything from their subjects, so every district would lack something. Good thing things aren't that way now, huh?

meaningMnemonic: A saw cuts into your heart and you are filled with fear . Well, you were filled with fear before the saw reached your heart too, but now that the saw is cutting into your heart, you’re feeling more fear than ever. Hints Try and imagine this saw slicing into your heart. Are you filled with fear? You should be.
readingMnemonic: Even more so than your fear of dying, you are filled with the fear that you’ll never get to vacation in きょう と . You always wanted to take a trip to きょうと , but if you die from this saw wound to the heart, you’ll never get the chance to go. Hints I fear you’ll never make it to きょうと . Think of きょうと and how you long for it as you slowly die from that saw wound to the heart.

meaningMnemonic: An animal eats a child from a plate in a very fierce manner. This is a fierce animal, so it makes sense that it would eat the child in a fierce style. Hints See the fierce animal fiercely eating the child from the plate. It’s very gruesome. See blood and body parts flying everywhere as the animal devours the child.
readingMnemonic: The reason this fierce animal is eating the child from the plate is because the child forgot to mow ( もう ) the animal’s lawn. The fierce animal had hired the child to mow his lawn today, and when the child forgot to do it, the fierce animal hunted the child down and ate him. Hints That child really shouldn’t have forgotten to mow the lawn. Imagine you are the child, being eaten by the fierce animal and wishing that you would have just mowed the lawn like you said you would.

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami rolls in and destroys all the construction that was being done on the inlet and the bay . Both the inlet and the bay were having a lot of construction done on them to repair the damage from the last tsunami, and then another tsunami rolled in and destroyed all that too. Bummer. Hints Picture all the construction on the bay and the inlet getting destroyed by the tsunami. Look at all of it fall apart and crash to the ground as the tsunami knocks it down. Imagine yourself right near the action, feeling the water spray from the tsunami.
readingMnemonic: Imagine the Japanese people standing on the bay and the inlet as the tsunami approaches. “ Eh ( え )? What is that, Akiko?” “Eh? Where? Oh gawd, it’s a tsunami!!” Hints EH? A tsunami you say? Those construction areas are screwed, man. Again, imagine the tsunami demolishing the area. Then be all like, “Eh? A tsunami? Aw, man.”

meaningMnemonic: In the morning , Korea will still be Korea . Hints Picture Korea first thing in the morning. You can see all the cities, the countryside, everything waking up.
readingMnemonic: You know who was a big fan of Korea ? Genghis Khan ( かん ). He liked Korea so much that he totally ignored it while he was subjugating the crap out of the rest of Asia. Hints Sadly for Korea, the later Khans wouldn't be quite as kind (looking at you, Ögedei, Güyük, and Möngke). They liked Korea too, but they showed their love a little more… aggressively.

meaningMnemonic: The narwhal is meeting in private with the turkey so they can, uh, show each other some private things. Doing this they realize they're both male ! You gotta be pretty manly and brave to do something like that. Hints Picture a male narwhal and a male turkey meeting together in private. Whispering. Giggling. Pointing at each other's male bits, each admiring how manly and brave the other is.
readingMnemonic: These male animals are obviously experimenting with things still. Ah, they must be you ths ( ゆう )!  To be a youth, again! Hints It's just nature. Youths like to learn and try new things. And if two male youth animals wanna get together in private that's their business.

meaningMnemonic: The radical means mysterious and the kanji means the same thing: mysterious . It can also mean dark , 'cause mysterious things tend to be kinda dark and shadowy. Hints When's the last time you saw something bright and mysterious? Never, I bet.
readingMnemonic: There is no one more mysterious than Gen ji ( げん ). He's tall, dark , handsome, and most of all... 〜 mysterious 〜 ! Hints Who's the mysterious man who's always reciting poetry? Genji! Who's the mysterious man who gets all the ladies? Genji! Who's the mysterious man looking all dark and depressed because someone turned him down? G... Genji…

meaningMnemonic: On every boat there is a lid on the table that's used for navigation . When you take the lid off, there is a big map, a sextant, and some little boat miniatures. All the navigation tools. Hints You forget to put the lid back on the navigation station and all those tools and boat pieces go flying around the boat and into the water. Oops.
readingMnemonic: You watch the navigation equipment roll away and then you feel a slap on the back of your head. Ouch! You turn around and there stands こう いち , who you took with you as the navigator of this expedition. And, you just lost all his stuff! Hints Picture this seafaring こういち angrily chasing you around the ruined navigation station, trying to hit you with a telescope.

meaningMnemonic: To the servant you say: " gun , ground , plate ." It is your job to oversee everything they do. Hints You point to the gun. You point to the ground (that's where the gun goes). You point to the plate (you want it). You have to oversee everything the servant does.
readingMnemonic: Why must you oversee everything? Because you are Genghis Khan ( かん ), and Genghis Khan oversees everything. Hints If anyone had to oversee a lot, it was Genghis Khan, who had one of the largest kingdoms in all of history.

meaningMnemonic: There’s an arrow in that turkey and you do everything in your power to recommend that we don’t eat the turkey. There’s an arrow in this turkey. The arrow looks a little broken, so there’s probably splinters all up inside that turkey. I know you’re all hungry but I can’t recommend eating this bird. Hints You can’t recommend this turkey. It’s probably dangerous. Imagine sending this turkey back in a restaurant, very upset with everything. Also keep in mind that the arrow is half buried in the turkey and looks a little broken since the arrow radical is a bit off.
readingMnemonic: You recommend the Genghis Khan ( かん ) special instead of this arrow-tainted turkey! When it comes out, your heart sinks. Genghis Khan apparently ate a cow with an arrow broken off in it. Hints Welp, I guess if Genghis Khan recommends eating food with weapons still in them, you're okay with recommending it too. Eat up, everyone.

meaningMnemonic: Under this roof you jackhammer your religion into people. Hints It's a religion building. They have a lot of different names, churches, mosques, temples, cathedrals, but none of those matter. All that matters is that you really drill whichever religion you want into the heads of the people who come under your roof.
readingMnemonic: Your religion requires everyone to take off their shoe s ( しゅう ). Mostly because the shoes will help them resist the jackhammering, so you tell them that to join your religion they have to leave their shoes at the door. Hints Picture the pile of shoes left outside. If you see a bunch of shoes like this you can be sure there's a religious place around here.

meaningMnemonic: If what you say comes out blue , everyone knows that means you made a request . You request a favor and the words slide out of your mouth in a bright, blue blob. They hover in front of you for a few seconds, before splashing onto the person you made the request to. Hints Picture this blue, slimy request. You could have done that thing by yourself, but you requested it of someone else, and now it's all over and everyone can see it.
readingMnemonic: The next time someone request s something from you, take out your sa ber ( せい ) and slice it in half! Hints Now they have the blue request gunk on them, and you can walk away as your already-blue sword absorbs the rest. Oh, and you don't have to fulfill the request (bonus!).

meaningMnemonic: The soul of a narwhal was sucked into its towel , which is scary ! Hints Watch as the narwhal's face contorts as you see its soul get slurped out by the towel it was using.
readingMnemonic: As you watch this scary scene you can't help but mutter, " Foo l," ( ふ ) under your breath. Then you hear "Fool, fool, fool, it's too scary you fool!" and you realize all of the other narwhals are chanting. Hints You don't know what's more scary. That the narwhal's soul got sucked out, or that all of its kind is calling it a fool now that it's dead.

meaningMnemonic: There is a cross in your forehead with a thread attached to it, forcing you to search where it leads. You’re not sure how the cross got stuck in your forehead, but you are interested in seeing where this piece of thread leads. The search is on. Hints It hurts to have this cross stuck in your forehead, but try to ignore that as you search for where the thread leads. Imagine gathering the thread in your hands as you move along.
readingMnemonic: Your search is over. You found the end of the thread. The thread leads you to a sack ( さく ). A sack filled with more crosses with more threads attached to them. What does it all mean!?! Hints Why are there more crosses and threads in the sack? Are you supposed to take them from the sack and throw them at other people’s foreheads? Maybe. Imagine yourself reaching into the sack and throwing the crosses at other people.

meaningMnemonic: The servant radical and the servant kanji are exactly the same! Just remember that the kanji also means retainer and you’ll be fine. Hints Retainer and servant are basically the same thing, so remembering this one shouldn’t be too hard for you.
readingMnemonic: Your servant , also known as your retainer , bangs his shins ( しん ) all the time so you make him wear jean s ( じん ) to work now. He bangs his shins on all the furniture in the house, knocking over all your valuables. But at least when he’s wearing jeans it doesn’t leave bruises like it did when he wasn’t wearing pants. Hints Imagine your servant banging his shins on everything in your house. Hand him a pair of jeans and tell him to put them on to soften the blows.

meaningMnemonic: The leader of the mountain turkey s is our sponsor . He's paying us to say and type everything you're reading. Hints This message is brought to you by our generous sponsor, the leader of the mountain turkeys. Long may he reign.
readingMnemonic: This same sponsor is also how you made your cy borg ( さい ). You didn't think you were able to get all those body parts yourself, did you? No no, the leader of the mountain turkeys sponsored you so you could do your experiments. Hints Turn your cyborg over and you'll see a stamp under one of its feet. It says, "Sponsored by" with a little picture of a turkey on top a mountain.

meaningMnemonic: If dirt and more dirt is all you see as you go from place to place, you must be roaming the streets of a city . Cities are notoriously dirty places, so watch your step when you head out into the streets. Hints Imagine yourself caked in dirt as you make your way through this urban jungle — someone really needs to clean up these streets!
readingMnemonic: As you roam the streets , brushing the dirt off yourself, a guy ( がい ) bumps into you: "Hey guy, watch where you're going!" As he says this he bumps into another guy. "Whoa there, guy — you think you own these streets or somethin'?" "As a matter of fact, my guy, I run these streets, so you'd better check yourself." Hints These two guys seem like they might be wise guys, so you hightail it out of there. You don't want to be another victim to the streets.

meaningMnemonic: Say good luck to one person enough and they'll be stuffed full of that luck. Hints Better safe than sorry. Don't just say good luck once, make sure they're stuffed!
readingMnemonic: You stuffed them by saying good luck two ( つ ) whole times! Hints Picture a person with the actual words "good luck" stuffed into their body.

meaningMnemonic: The servant sits on a stool , holding a piece of thread , looking very tense . Hints You walk by this tense servant and pause for a moment. They raise their tense eyes up at you and you can see they're shaking.
readingMnemonic: You ask the servant why they're so tense , and they say they've been assigned to assassinate the Kin g ( きん ) of England with this piece of thread. Hints Imagine how tense you would be if you were about to try to murder the King! Your entire body would tense up, maybe to the point that you wouldn't be able to actually go through with it.

meaningMnemonic: At the gate , you kiss the cabinet members, one by one. In order to gain access to this government building, you have to kiss all the members of the cabinet at the gate. What a strange ritual. Hints Imagine kissing all the members of the cabinet. A lot of them are old men. Imagine kissing all of them at the gate. Eww.
readingMnemonic: You need to kiss each member of the cabinet to gain access to their building. And you need to get into the building to recover your cock ( かく ). Your prize winning cock has been captured by a member of the cabinet and you need to infiltrate their headquarters and recover your rooster! Hints Imagine yourself sneaking past the cabinet members, finding your cock, grabbing it, and getting out of there. You’ve recovered your rooster! The day is won.

meaningMnemonic: Your leader sees your bare foot and urge s you to put a sock on it. Hints Imagine your leader's face when he sees your bare foot, and just how emphatic he is as he urges you to put a sock on it. He's really worried your foot's going to get cold!
readingMnemonic: As urge d, you put a sock ( そく ) on your foot. Ahh, that feels so much better. What a great thing, this sock. Hints Feel this sock on your foot. It feels great. Wiggle your toes around inside the sock as you think about how glad you are that you did as your leader urged. Note that this kanji also has the same reading as 足 , so keep that in mind too!

meaningMnemonic: When a yakuza 's knife boil s, you know something very violent and intense is about to happen. Hints The yakuza member is so upset his knife boils. Right after, they will definitely get violent and intense.
readingMnemonic: When someone gets violent or intense , they always yell " Let's ( れつ ) get violent and intense!" Hints In the case of our mnemonic, it's a yakuza member getting violent. So, imagine a yakuza member saying "Ret's get violent!" before doing just that.

meaningMnemonic: Abbreviation in language is an abbreviation or an acronym .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 「高校」は「高等学校」の略語です。
sentences.english: "Kōkō" is an abbreviation of "kōtōgakkō (high school)."

sentences.japanese: 竹下さんはクリエイティブな略語を使って話すのが大好きです。
sentences.english: Takeshita-san loves to speak using creative abbreviations.

sentences.japanese: 最近の若者が使う略語は、難しすぎてよく分かりません。
sentences.english: I don't understand the abbreviations that young people use recently. They are too difficult.

sentences.japanese: 略語辞典を貸してもらえませんか？
sentences.english: Can I borrow your dictionary of acronyms and abbreviations?

meaningMnemonic: This word looks a lot like 怒る , doesn't it? But this word isn't a verb, so you can think of it as referring to anger or wrath itself.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you: I have a lot of anger because I ca rry ( いか ) all of my own things (books, luggage, drinks) and no one will ever carry them for me. Plus, the more things I carry, the more anger I carry inside. Ahh!

sentences.japanese: 私の怒りは三分以上続かない。
sentences.english: My wrath will not go on for more than three minutes.

sentences.japanese: 直子は和希の言葉にとてつもない怒りを覚えた。
sentences.english: Naoko felt intense anger at Kazuki's words.

sentences.japanese: 怒りって、後からフツフツわいてくることが多いよね。
sentences.english: Anger often bubbles up slowly after the fact, doesn't it?

meaningMnemonic: An angry energy comes out of you when you have anger . 怒気 looks simple, but it's a pretty advanced term more commonly used in literature, typically to describe a character's anger as expressed through their voices, facial expressions, attitudes, or the surrounding atmosphere.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 「よくそんな冷たいことが言えるよな！」と、コウイチは怒気をおびた声で言った。
sentences.english: "What a heartless thing to say!" said Koichi with anger in his voice.

sentences.japanese: 相手は、こちらの怒気を感じたのか、急に静かになった。
sentences.english: The other person suddenly grew quiet, perhaps sensing my anger.

sentences.japanese: なんとか怒気を隠そうとしたが、引きつった笑顔しか作れなかった。
sentences.english: I tried to hide my anger, but could only manage a strained smile.

sentences.japanese: 彼の鼻の穴は怒気を含んで膨らんでいる。
sentences.english: His nostrils swelled with anger.

meaningMnemonic: 痛い is "painful." This is the noun version, it is a pain or pain .
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as 痛い . No pain here.

sentences.japanese: 特に痛みはありません。
sentences.english: There's no pain in particular.

sentences.japanese: 子供には人の痛みが分かるような大人に育ってほしいです。
sentences.english: I hope that my kid will grow up to become an adult who understands others’ pain.

sentences.japanese: 胸にしこりみたいなものと痛みがあるんだけど、乳がん検査した方がいいかな？
sentences.english: I have a hard spot and pain in my breast. Should I have it examined for breast cancer?

sentences.japanese: 俺の伯母さん、クソしてる時に胸にするどい痛みが走って、119に電話したんだって。
sentences.english: Apparently, my aunt had a sharp pain in her chest while pooping and called 119.

meaningMnemonic: When you say humbly that you're request ing something, you're putting forward an application . 申請 refers to the process of officially applying for approval or permission, like ビザの申請 (application for a visa), ライセンスの申請 (application for a license), or 休暇の申請 (application for leave/vacation).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You already know this reading for 請 , but not for 申 , so here's a mnemonic to help you: Today you finally submitted your application for a new shin ( しん ). Your old one had to be painstakingly removed after you banged it against a table. Anyway, congrats on the application for your new shin!

sentences.english: application for permission

sentences.english: applicant

sentences.english: to accept applications

sentences.english: an application is required

sentences.japanese: 申請が通る
sentences.english: an application is approved

sentences.japanese: 申請が受理される
sentences.english: an application is accepted
