sentences.english: Oh no! I'd forgotten to apply for a visa.

sentences.japanese: 申請手続きに時間がかかってるんです。
sentences.english: The application process is taking quite a while to complete.

sentences.japanese: ようやく許可申請が受理されました！
sentences.english: At last, the application for permission has been accepted!

meaningMnemonic: The surface that accumulate s into one area is a particular area . This has to do with math. When you add all the surfaces together by accumulating them into one calculation, you get yourself the area!
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 長方形と正方形の面積を求める方法は同じですか。
sentences.english: Are the methods for calculating the area of a rectangle and a square the same?

sentences.japanese: コウイチの家の庭の面積はどれくらいですか？
sentences.english: How large of an area is Koichi's yard?

sentences.japanese: 彼のおでこの面積は100平方メートルある。
sentences.english: The area of his forehead is 100 square meters.

meaningMnemonic: Append and attach this document to your email. That’s called attachment . 添付 refers to the act of attaching something supplementary to another document, like attaching a file to an email or attaching a map to an invitation.
readingMnemonic: The reading for 添 is what you'd expect. The reading for 付 is the on'yomi reading ふ , which you've learned with 付近 . But for this word it becomes ぷ from the rendaku fairies. Just think of an attachment where instead of a document or something, you get an attachment of poo p ( ぷ ). What a gross attachment. Your friend who likes to send poop attachments is dumb.

sentences.japanese: コウイチの予定につきましては、添付のスケジュールをご確認ください。
sentences.english: As for Koichi's plans, please check the attached schedule.

sentences.japanese: WaniKaniのメールには、よく面白いGIFが添付されています。
sentences.english: WaniKani emails often have funny GIFs attached.

sentences.japanese: グリーンカード申請に必要な添付書類のリストはどこにありますか。
sentences.english: Where is the list of the necessary attached documents for a green card application?

sentences.japanese: 人事部長様、 恐れ入りますが、このEメールに添付された履歴書にお目通し頂けますでしょうか。お忙しいとは存じますが、よろしくお願い申し上げます。
sentences.english: Dear hiring manager, please have a look at the resume attached to this email. Thank you for your time.

meaningMnemonic: Navigation in the sky is aviation . Vroom vroom, sky flying! On its own 航空 refers to aviation, but you'll usually see it in compound words like 航空機 (aircraft) and 航空会社 (airline company).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 私は日本航空大学の航空工学科で、航空工学について学びました。
sentences.english: I studied aerospace engineering in the Department of Aerospace Engineering at Japan Aviation University.

sentences.japanese: アメリカから羽田空港の航空路線が増えてより便利になりました。
sentences.english: The number of flight routes from America to Haneda Airport increased and has made travel more convenient.

sentences.japanese: 私はいつもこのアプリを使って格安航空券をさがしています。
sentences.english: I always use this app to search for cheap airline tickets.

sentences.japanese: あの航空会社は四月に新路線を増やす予定だ。
sentences.english: That airline company is adding a new route in April.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. 宴 is an old-fashioned word for 宴会 . It refers to large, festive feasts in traditional settings, often involving lots of sake and the enjoyment of traditional performing arts. You may see it used in literature or in song lyrics to evoke scenes of grand, lavish banquets from ages past.
readingMnemonic: At a banquet or party , you don't only get food, you also 歌 GE T ( うたげ ), which is you getting a song from a singer. After all, entertainment is just as important as the food when you're at a wild bacchanal such as this!

sentences.japanese: 王子は、宴の最中に撃たれて死んだ。
sentences.english: The prince was shot dead during the feast.

sentences.japanese: こよいの宴は実に楽しいものですな。
sentences.english: The banquet this evening is truly fun, isn't it?

sentences.japanese: さぁ、宴じゃ宴じゃ！みんな、飲め飲め！
sentences.english: Alright, it's party time! Everyone, drink up, drink up!

meaningMnemonic: A banquet meet ing is when you meet together for a banquet or dinner party . 宴会 refers to a gathering where people share food and drinks to celebrate something or deepen their social bonds. It's generally not used for casual dinner parties among friends, but rather for formal or semi-formal social events involving a larger group of people, such as farewell parties for colleagues or workplace holiday parties.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 今度の宴会の幹事をすることになりました。
sentences.english: I'm going to be the organizer of the next banquet.

sentences.japanese: 忘年会のための宴会場を予約しなくてはいけません。
sentences.english: I need to reserve a banquet hall for the year-end party.

sentences.japanese: 仕事の締めくくりをつけてから、宴会に参加しました。
sentences.english: I joined the dinner party after wrapping up my work.

sentences.japanese: 宴会で嫌な奴とお酒を飲むのは、会議で議事録を記録するより退屈な仕事だ。
sentences.english: Drinking alcohol with someone you don’t like at a dinner party is a much more tedious task than recording the proceedings of a meeting.

meaningMnemonic: A beckoning cat is a beckoning cat or maneki neko . 招き猫 are the cat statues believed to bring good luck and fortune to their owners. They're often placed in front of shops with one paw raised, as if beckoning and saying, "Hey, come on in!"
readingMnemonic: This word uses the kun'yomi readings for both kanji, which you know already!

sentences.japanese: 電動招き猫のコンセント、	さしっぱなしにしないでね。
sentences.english: Don't leave the electrical Maneki Neko plugged into the outlet.

sentences.japanese: もっとワニカニが売れるように、トーフグオフィスに招き猫を買いました。
sentences.english: We purchased a maneki neko for the Tofugu office to improve WaniKani sales.

sentences.japanese: お店によく置かれている招き猫は、左手を上げています。これは、左手が「お客さんを招く」とされているためです。
sentences.english: The maneki neko often seen in stores is raising its left paw, since the left hand is believed to "beckon customers."

sentences.japanese: 一方、右手を上げている招き猫は「お金や幸運を招く」とされているので、オフィスや個人宅にかざられることが多いです。
sentences.english: On the other hand, a maneki neko with its right paw raised is said to "beckon money and good fortune," so they are often displayed in offices or homes.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Note that 腹 can be considered a bit rougher or less polite compared to お腹 .
readingMnemonic: If anyone tries to touch your belly , that's hara ssment ( はら ). Unless you're cool with it, obviously. But if you're not, make sure to yell "harassment!" when they touch your belly. You should also shout what kind of harassment it is: 腹ハラ ( 腹 harassment). Note: This word will often get rendaku'd when it's combined with other vocab, like in ビールばら (beer belly) or 別ばら (separate stomach for dessert).

sentences.japanese: 腹をみたす
sentences.english: to fill one's stomach

sentences.japanese: 腹をかかえる
sentences.english: to hold one's stomach

sentences.japanese: 腹を立てる
sentences.english: to get angry

sentences.japanese: 腹をくくる
sentences.english: to steel oneself, to harden one's resolve

sentences.japanese: 腹を割る
sentences.english: to be frank, to be candid

sentences.japanese: お前ちょっと腹が出てきたんじゃねぇか？
sentences.english: You're starting to get a bit of a gut, aren't you?

sentences.japanese: 島崎さんは腹をかかえて笑っていました。
sentences.english: Ms. Shimazaki was holding her belly with laughter.

sentences.japanese: 最近ビール腹が気になって、とうとうダイエットをすることにしました。
sentences.english: I've been feeling self-conscious about my beer belly lately, so I finally decided to try to slim down.

sentences.japanese: ここ最近、ずっと腹が痛いんだ。
sentences.english: My stomach's been hurting nonstop lately.

meaningMnemonic: That's very odd and strange , making it bizarre and peculiar . 奇妙 is often used in literature to describe something that feels unusually strange or odd . It describes something being an almost otherworldly quality, sparking curiosity because it's so bizarre.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 『世にも奇妙な物語』っていう番組、知ってる？
sentences.english: Do you know the show called "Tales of the Unusual"?

sentences.japanese: 私の好きなマンガは『ジョジョの奇妙な冒険』です。
sentences.english: My favorite manga is "JoJo's Bizarre Adventure".

sentences.japanese: 遠くから聞こえてくる足音には、奇妙な規則性があり、それがかえって不気味だった。
sentences.english: The distant footsteps carried a peculiar rhythm, which only added to their eerie nature.

meaningMnemonic: A black board is a blackboard .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: まだ黒板を消さないでください。
sentences.english: Please don't erase what's on the blackboard yet.

sentences.japanese: 誰ですか、黒板消しを教室のとびらの間にはさんで落としたのは？
sentences.english: Who is it that wedged the blackboard eraser between the classroom door and made it fall?

sentences.japanese: うちの高校では、電子黒板を使った授業を取り入れています。
sentences.english: At our high school, we've incorporated lessons using electronic blackboards.

sentences.japanese: 黒板が使えないので、ホワイトボードを持参しています。
sentences.english: We can’t use the blackboard so I’ll bring in a whiteboard.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. 板 generally refers to something thin, flat, and solid, like a board, plank, slab, or plate. In some contexts, it can also refer to stock market boards that display trading prices, or bulletin boards used for posting messages in online forums.
readingMnemonic: Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Who can make good use of various board s? An avid eater ( いた )! If you’re an avid eater, you’ll need lots of (cutting) boards to prepare all the delicious food you’re going to eat. This makes boards and eaters the perfect match.

sentences.japanese: ノコギリで木の板を切りました。
sentences.english: I cut a wooden plank with a saw.

sentences.japanese: このプラスチックの板、何に使うの？
sentences.english: What are you going to use this plastic board for?

sentences.japanese: この置物に合う大理石の板をさがしています。
sentences.english: I'm looking for a marble board that matches this ornament.

sentences.japanese: 2chの野球板に書き込みをしたんですが、板違いだと言われてしまいました。
sentences.english: I posted some comments on a forum about baseball on 2chan, but I was told it was the wrong board.

meaningMnemonic: The big abbreviation is where you take everything and abbreviate it down to show the big picture. This abbreviation is the broad outline of something bigger. 大略 is a relatively formal word commonly found in writing. It generally refers to a broader, rougher outline or overview rather than a detailed summary.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 大略でいいので、会議の内容を教えてくれませんか？
sentences.english: Just a rough summary is fine, so can you tell me what the meeting was about?

sentences.japanese: まずは事件の大略を説明してくれないか？
sentences.english: Can you explain the outline of the incident first?

sentences.japanese: 彼の話の大略は理解できたけど、細かい部分はまだよく分かりません。
sentences.english: I understood the gist of his story, but I'm still unclear on the details.

sentences.japanese: この企画の大略は決まったので、次は詳細を詰めていきましょう。
sentences.english: The broad outline of this project has been decided, so let's work out the details next.

meaningMnemonic: A government colleague is someone who works for the bureaucracy , making them a bureaucrat . Just like the word bureaucracy in English, 官僚 often carries a negative connotation, suggesting red tape, inefficiency, or the power and influence that senior civil servants might wield within the government.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 彼は官僚出身だけど、腰が低くていいやつだよ。
sentences.english: He comes from a bureaucratic background, but he's humble and a good guy.

sentences.japanese: きっとアイツらみんな、我々キャリア官僚が天下りするのは当然の権利だとか思ってるんじゃない？
sentences.english: I'm sure they all think something like, "It's our rightful privilege as career bureaucrats to secure cushy post-retirement jobs."

sentences.japanese: 大きくなった国家に必ず官僚主義がはびこるように、大きくなった組織は、みんな大企業病にかかるんです。いわゆる官僚組織ってやつですよ。
sentences.english: Just as bureaucratism inevitably spreads in a large nation, every large organization ends up suffering from what we call "big company syndrome." It's what you might refer to as a bureaucratic organization.

meaningMnemonic: When the cabinet meets for deliberation they are having a cabinet meeting . So governmenty.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: これはもう閣議決定されたことです。
sentences.english: This was already decided in the cabinet meeting.

sentences.japanese: 昨日のデジタル相の閣議後の会見、見ましたか？
sentences.english: Did you watch the Digital Minister's press conference after yesterday's cabinet meeting?

sentences.japanese: さっきの閣議では何が議題だったんだっけ？忘れちゃった。
sentences.english: What did we discuss at the cabinet meeting held earlier today? I forgot.

sentences.japanese: 今回の閣議では閣僚のほぼ全員が反対に回った。
sentences.english: Most of the cabinet members cast an opposing vote at this cabinet meeting.

meaningMnemonic: The cabinet colleague s are the cabinet ministers or cabinet secretaries . They're the people in the Cabinet who are all colleagues with each other, making them cabinet members . Depending on the country, they're also called ministers or secretaries. 閣僚 is a formal term that refers to the collective group of high-ranking officials in a cabinet, but it can sometimes refer to an individual cabinet member as well.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 閣僚たちは、みんな反対しています。
sentences.english: All of the cabinet ministers are opposed.

sentences.japanese: 閣僚会議は月1回ですよ。
sentences.english: The cabinet meeting is held once a month.

sentences.japanese: 内部告発者により、この件に関する閣僚間のやりとりが明るみに出ました。
sentences.english: An internal whistleblower revealed the communication between the cabinet ministers regarding this issue.

meaningMnemonic: The middle part of Europe is Central Europe , wherever that is.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 中欧の国だったら、チェコに行ってみたいです。
sentences.english: Among Central European countries, I would like to visit the Czech Republic.

sentences.japanese: ドイツは西欧だと思っていたんですが、中欧の国の一つだったんですね。
sentences.english: I had been thinking that Germany was a part of Western Europe, but it was actually one of the Central European countries, wasn't it?

sentences.japanese: この夏は、中欧をひとり旅してきました。
sentences.english: This summer, I took a solo trip through Central Europe.

sentences.japanese: 中欧を旅してみたいなと随分長い間思っていたんですよ。
sentences.english: I’ve wanted to travel around Central Europe for a really long time.

meaningMnemonic: When something collapse s and break s, it is when a collapse happens. Something big collapsing or falling down will probably result in its destruction . 倒壊 is a formal word often found in news or official documents. It's used to describe buildings or structures collapsing, usually from destructive forces like natural disasters or bombings.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 今、『テロでロンドンブリッジ倒壊』のテロップが流れてきたよ！本当かな？
sentences.english: I just saw a news ticker saying "London Bridge collapses due to a terror attack"! Could it be true?

sentences.japanese: 大地震の影響で東京タワーが倒壊するかもしれないとの報道があった。
sentences.english: There were reports that Tokyo Tower might collapse due to the impact of the major earthquake.

sentences.japanese: 消防隊は、倒壊したビルの中から少女を助け出した。
sentences.english: The fire-fighting team rescued a girl from the collapsed building.

sentences.japanese: 私の祖父母の家はとても古いので、雪の重みで倒壊しかねません。
sentences.english: My grandparents' house is so old that it could collapse under the weight of the snow.

meaningMnemonic: We work at the same place and are colleague s, making us colleague s or coworker s. As you might guess from the 同 kanji, 同僚 generally refers to people working in the same workplace with the same rank or status. In other words, you wouldn't usually call your boss your 同僚 !
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: こちらは同僚の林さんです。
sentences.english: This is my colleague, Hayashi-san.

sentences.japanese: オレの同僚は冷たいヤツなんだよ。
sentences.english: My colleague is a cold-hearted man.

sentences.japanese: 困ったときに相談できるような上司や同僚だったら良かったんだけどね。
sentences.english: It would have been nice to have a boss or colleagues to turn to for advice when there was trouble.

meaningMnemonic: When all of something breaks , every last bit of it is broken. It's complete destruction !!! 全壊 is a formal term used when buildings or structures are completely destroyed by disasters like earthquakes, fires, or accidents. It's often seen in news reports or insurance assessments to describe the total destruction of property.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 全壊したビルの中から何か出てきました。
sentences.english: Something came out of the completely destroyed building.

sentences.japanese: マイホームを持っていたんですが、台風で全壊しちゃったんですよ。
sentences.english: I had my own house, but it was completely destroyed by the typhoon.

sentences.japanese: トルネードで自宅はほぼ全壊ですが、家族はみんな元気です。
sentences.english: Our house was almost totally destroyed by the tornado, but my family is all safe.

sentences.japanese: この地震で被害を受けた家のうち、全壊家屋は全部で835戸だった。
sentences.english: Among the houses that suffered from this earthquake, the number of completely destroyed houses was 835.

meaningMnemonic: When you draw near to give something, you are probably giving a contribution . 寄与 is a very formal word that refers to significant contributions in professional or official settings. It's commonly used in academic or business contexts to highlight how someone's work contributes to the advancement of a field of study or the growth of a company.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 後進国の発展に寄与したとして、ノーベル賞が授与された。
sentences.english: The Nobel Prize was awarded to them for their contribution to the development of less developed countries.

sentences.japanese: トーフグが世界平和に寄与していることを知っているかい？
sentences.english: Did you know that Tofugu is contributing to world peace?

sentences.japanese: フィンランドの作曲家であるジャン・シベリウス は、音楽を通じて、国民意識の形成に多大な寄与をしました。
sentences.english: The Finnish composer Jean Sibelius made a significant contribution to the formation of national identity through his music.

sentences.japanese: 地域への寄与度が高いビジネスの方が、助成金は下りやすいんです。
sentences.english: Businesses that contribute more to the local community tend to receive grants more easily.

sentences.japanese: プロジェクトのコスト削減への寄与と納品日数短縮をもたらした服部さんにプロジェクトマネージャー賞が贈られた。
sentences.english: A project manager award was given to Ms. Hattori for her contributions to cost reductions and the shortening of delivery times for goods in the project.

meaningMnemonic: You like it because it gives you an odd feeling in your heart . You don't quite know what it is you like, but that's because it's curiosity that you have.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: サトシ君は好奇心いっぱいですね！
sentences.english: Satoshi is full of curiosity, isn't he!

sentences.japanese: 最近好奇心が刺激されるような経験してないなー。
sentences.english: These days, I don't experience anything that stimulates my curiosity.

sentences.japanese: ウォータースライダーでびしょびしょにぬれてしまい、他の人から好奇心に満ちた目で見られた。
sentences.english: I got soaked on the water slide, and people were looking at me with curious eyes.

sentences.japanese: 子どもの頃、私は好奇心旺盛でした。
sentences.english: When I was a child I was full of curiosity.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. 娘 primarily means daughter but can also refer to a young woman (often unmarried). This is because its original form is 産す女 ( むすめ ), or "a woman who gives birth." Over time, it came to represent both daughters and young women.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji.

sentences.japanese: 私には娘が三人います。
sentences.english: I have three daughters.

sentences.japanese: 松本さんのとこの娘さん、今年大学生になるんだって！
sentences.english: I heard Matsumoto's daughter is going to be a university student this year!

sentences.japanese: こんな時間に若い娘さんたちだけで歩いてたら危ないよ？
sentences.english: It's dangerous for young women to be walking around at this time of night, you know?

sentences.japanese: 「私の娘は人魚なんだ。」「ええっ、それってつまり、あんた魚と結婚したってことか？」
sentences.english: "My daughter is a mermaid." "Whoa! Does that mean you married a fish?"

meaningMnemonic: Things 締める (tighten), and eventually 切る (cut off), meaning you’ve reached the deadline ! You can associate this with the feeling of your chest tightening once you approach the due date for something. Note that you'll often encounter this written with okurigana like 締め切り as well. You might even see it with a simplified version of the 締 kanji written 〆切 , which is relatively common in handwriting!
readingMnemonic: The reading for this is the stem form of both verbs, so 締め ( しめ ) and 切り ( きり ), put together!

sentences.japanese: 締切はいつですか？
sentences.english: When is the deadline?

sentences.japanese: 申込の締切日は三日後です。
sentences.english: The application deadline is in three days.

sentences.japanese: このままじゃ締切に間に合わないかもしれない。
sentences.english: At this rate, I might not make the deadline.

sentences.japanese: うまく締切を明日まで延ばせたの？
sentences.english: Did you have any luck with putting the deadline off till tomorrow?

meaningMnemonic: To diagnose is to (metaphorically) cut off all the possibilities you don't believe to be likely. That's how you get a diagnosis ! 診断 is primarily used in medical contexts to mean the act of diagnosing or the diagnosis itself. In non-medical contexts, it can also mean an assessment used to evaluate something, like a 性格診断 (personality test).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: どうしてその診断結果になったのか、診断のプロセスを説明してもらえませんか？
sentences.english: Could you explain the process of how you came to that diagnosis?

sentences.japanese: MBTI診断っていう性格診断テスト、知ってる？
sentences.english: Do you know the personality test called MBTI assessment?

sentences.japanese: 西村医師は乳がんの診断においては右に出る者はいないと言われています。
sentences.english: Doctor Nishimura is believed to be the best doctor in terms of their diagnosis of breast cancer.

sentences.japanese: 私の息子は四歳の時に喘息だと診断されました。
sentences.english: My son was diagnosed with asthma when he was four.

meaningMnemonic: If you draw near someone and attach some stuff to them, you're making a donation . They get to keep it, after all. 寄付 means donating money, goods, or resources, usually for a charitable purpose.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: もしよろしければワニカニに寄付をお願いできますか。
sentences.english: If possible, may I ask you for a donation to WaniKani?

sentences.japanese: 毎年少しだけ、母校へお金を寄付しています。
sentences.english: I contribute a little money to my alma mater every year.

sentences.japanese: このサイトは、寄付金で運営しているものなんです。
sentences.english: This site is run through donations.

sentences.japanese: 金持ちが多額の寄付をするのは、節税のためだよ。
sentences.english: Wealthy people make large donations mainly for tax-saving purposes.

meaningMnemonic: Sometimes even though you think you're very much awake and alive , you can't help fall into a sleep and start dozing off . But you're not dead! You're totally alive, so let's hope no one thinks you're doing anything other than nodding off . 居眠り refers to light, unintentional sleep. It often happens when someone is supposed to stay awake but dozes off due to tiredness or boredom, like during a meeting, class, or (heaven forbid) while driving.
readingMnemonic: This word combines the kun'yomi readings from 居る and 眠る , both of which you've learned, so you should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 授業中に居眠りして先生に怒られた。
sentences.english: I dozed off during class and the teacher got mad at me.

sentences.japanese: 運転中に居眠りしてたみたいなんだ。
sentences.english: It seems like they dozed off while driving.

sentences.japanese: 仕事中に居眠りしてしまったけど、誰にも気づかれなかった。
sentences.english: I nodded off during work, but no one noticed.

sentences.japanese: 国会議員の会議中の居眠り対策について、政府は国民に意見を募っている。
sentences.english: The government is seeking public opinions on measures to prevent members of parliament from falling asleep during meetings.

meaningMnemonic: The dry seasons is the dry season . 乾季 is a formal term typically used in geographical climate discussions, especially for regions with clear wet and dry seasons like Southeast Asia, Africa, and South America.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: ここは今、乾季の真っ最中です。
sentences.english: Currently it's the height of the dry season here.

sentences.japanese: フィリピンに旅行に行くなら乾季がオススメですよ。
sentences.english: I recommend going during the dry season if you are planning to travel to the Philippines.

sentences.japanese: この地域では、乾季が5月から10月まで続きます。
sentences.english: In this region, the dry season lasts from May to October.

sentences.japanese: いつもはこの時期は既に乾季になっているが、今年は未だ雨が降り続けている。
sentences.english: By now it's usually the dry season already, but it still continues to rain this year.

meaningMnemonic: The bay door isn't what you might think, it refers to Edo , which is what Tokyo was called back in the day. You'll still see references to it everywhere, though, so it's good to learn. You can also call this Tokyo if you want, but I'd prefer if you answered "Edo," instead.
readingMnemonic: The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji. Just watch out for that rendaku on 戸 , which changes the reading to ど . Of course, it will be easy if you already know the word Edo !

sentences.japanese: 江戸時代は約260年間続きました。
sentences.english: The Edo period lasted for about 260 years.

sentences.japanese: 江戸前ずしの特徴を教えてください。
sentences.english: Please tell me the characteristics of Edo-style sushi.

sentences.japanese: この博物館では江戸時代の町の様子を再現したジオラマが見ものです。
sentences.english: The highlight of this museum is a diorama recreating what towns looked like in the Edo period.

sentences.japanese: だらだらしてないで、さっさと二階に行って宿題をしなさい。日本の江戸時代についてレポートを書かないといけないって言ってたでしょ！
sentences.english: Stop mucking around and go upstairs and do your homework. You said you gotta write an essay about the Edo period in Japan, right?

meaningMnemonic: Something's effective power is its effectiveness . If it has effective power, it remains in effect . This word usually refers to the legal force or effectiveness of a law, agreement, contract, or treaty, but it can also be used to talk about the efficacy of other things, such as medicine.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: その条約は明日で効力を失う。
sentences.english: That treaty will cease to be in effect from tomorrow.

sentences.japanese: あなたの今日のプレゼンテーションは、前回に比べて効力が少し弱いような気がしました。
sentences.english: Your presentation today seemed like it was a bit weaker in its effectiveness compared to the last one.

sentences.japanese: この薬を飲むと、あなたは空を飛べるようになります。でも、飛んでいる時に薬の効力が切れると大変なので、気をつけてくださいね。
sentences.english: If you take this medicine, you will be able to fly in the sky. However, please be careful because if the effect of the medicine wears off while you are flying, it could be very dangerous.

sentences.japanese: 調停が成立したときに作成される調停調書は、判決と同様の効力を有します。
sentences.english: When a mediation agreement is reached, the mediation report created thereafter holds the same legal effect as a court judgment.

meaningMnemonic: The most mysterious thing that's connected to a house is the entranceway . When you're walking into one you never know what's coming next. You just take off your shoes and hope the rest of the house isn't really weird or something. If it is, the entryway is then your only way out.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 玄関のところで待ってますね！
sentences.english: I'll be waiting by the entryway!

sentences.japanese: 玄関のドアにヒビが入ったので、修理が必要です。
sentences.english: There's a crack in the foyer’s door, so it needs to be repaired.

sentences.japanese: 彼は玄関で傘をたたんでから、家の中に入りました。
sentences.english: He folded his umbrella at the entranceway before stepping into the house.

sentences.japanese: 玄関で靴を脱いでください。
sentences.english: Please take off your shoes in the entranceway.

meaningMnemonic: You have Europe and America . This word refers to Europe and America . When people use 欧米 in Japan, they usually mean Western countries in general ( the West ), including North America and Western Europe. You'll often see it in news reports related to Western countries or in topics comparing Japanese and Western cultures, customs, or trends.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 日本の食べ物は欧米でも人気があります。
sentences.english: Japanese food is popular even in the West.

sentences.japanese: このホテルの主なお客様は、欧米の方々なんです。
sentences.english: The hotel's main customers are Westerners.

sentences.japanese: 「欧米」に含まれる国を全部挙げることができますか。
sentences.english: Can you name all the countries included in "Europe and the US"?

sentences.japanese: 欧米でピンクのバラを栽培している所がないか探しているんですが。
sentences.english: I'm searching for a place in Europe and America that grows pink roses.

meaningMnemonic: 極める is "to carry to extremes." So, 極めて is something similar. It's used to refer to something that's extremely _______.
readingMnemonic: The reading comes from 極める .

sentences.japanese: この問題は極めて重要です。
sentences.english: This issue is extremely important.

sentences.japanese: この薬は副作用が極めて少ないです。
sentences.english: This medicine has extremely few side effects.

sentences.japanese: 我々は、極めて危険な状況に直面しています。
sentences.english: We are facing an extremely dangerous situation.

sentences.japanese: 君がこの問題の解決方法について具体的には何も考えていないというのは、極めて明白な事実だ。
sentences.english: It’s extremely obvious that you don’t have any idea how we can solve this problem.

meaningMnemonic: Your fever turns violent when you express your fervent feelings. 熱烈 is a relatively formal word that describes someone being fervently absorbed in something or someone and showing ardent or passionate behavior, like 熱烈に応援する (support fervently).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 熱烈なファン
sentences.english: ardent fan

sentences.japanese: 熱烈な支持者
sentences.english: fervent supporter

sentences.japanese: 熱烈なアプローチ
sentences.english: passionate approach

sentences.japanese: 熱烈なキス
sentences.english: passionate kiss

sentences.japanese: 熱烈なラブレター
sentences.english: impassioned love letter

sentences.japanese: 熱烈に支持する
sentences.english: to ardently support

sentences.japanese: 熱烈に応援する
sentences.english: to fervently cheer

sentences.japanese: 熱烈にアピールする
sentences.english: to passionately appeal

sentences.japanese: 熱烈にアプローチする
sentences.english: to passionately approach

sentences.japanese: そのバンドの熱烈なファンが会場をいっぱいにしていた。
sentences.english: The venue was filled with passionate fans of the band.

sentences.japanese: 彼からの熱烈なラブレターに感動して、付き合うことにしたんです。
sentences.english: I was moved by his impassioned love letter, and decided to start dating him.

sentences.japanese: 彼はその作家の作品を熱烈に支持している。
sentences.english: He is a fervent supporter of that author's works.

sentences.japanese: その女性は、「トーフグの熱烈なファンなんです」と言って、コウイチに熱烈なキスをした。
sentences.english: The woman said, "I'm an ardent fan of Tofugu," and gave Koichi a passionate kiss.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. You can put this on other words to say that it's a " Fierce ____" or " Intense _____," or something along those lines. If you see this, you know that something is being done really fiercely or intensely. 猛 is used in compounds to emphasize fierceness or intensity, like 猛暑 (intense heat) or 猛勉強 (intense studying). It can also be used in expressions like 猛アプローチ (relentlessly pursuing someone romantically — a fierce "approach"). In casual uses like this, the strong tone is often intentionally goofy or comical.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji, probably because it's stuck onto things making it all jukugo and such.

sentences.japanese: 彼は猛勉強して、大学に合格しました。
sentences.english: He studied fiercely and passed the university entrance exam.

sentences.japanese: 猛ふぶきで雪が三メートル程積もりました。
sentences.english: A fierce blizzard piled up about three meters of snow.

sentences.japanese: あの犬、急に猛ダッシュしてきたからびっくりしたよ！
sentences.english: That dog suddenly dashed at me fiercely, and I was shocked!

sentences.japanese: バイクが猛スピードで突っ込んできた。
sentences.english: The motorcycle came rushing forward at breakneck speed.

meaningMnemonic: If you're fierce and violent then you are fierce and violent . 猛烈 is used to describe intense things, like fierce storms, or actions done with great intensity, like working like mad. Its strong tone can feel a bit comical in casual use, so people also use it playfully to exaggerate things like how hungry they feel.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 彼は猛烈なスピードで仕事を終わらせました。
sentences.english: He finished the work at an intense speed.

sentences.japanese: 彼女は猛烈に勉強して、試験に合格しました。
sentences.english: She studied intensely and passed the exam.

sentences.japanese: 昨日のライブ、猛烈に楽しかった！
sentences.english: Yesterday's concert was ferociously fun!

sentences.japanese: このプロジェクトのリーダーを買って出たことを、今猛烈に後悔しています。
sentences.english: I seriously regret that I volunteered to be the leader of this project now.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 履く is "to put on shoes" and 物 means "thing"? Well, combine them and you have a word for things you put on your feet — footwear or shoes , in other words. You might know 履く is used for lots of different clothes worn below the waist, but be careful: 履き物 only refers to footwear and shoes.
readingMnemonic: This uses kun'yomi readings you learned with the vocab words 履く and 物 . If you can remember those you'll be good to go.

sentences.japanese: 履き物を脱ぐ
sentences.english: to take off footwear

sentences.japanese: 履き物を履く
sentences.english: to put on footwear

sentences.japanese: 履き物をそろえる
sentences.english: to line up footwear, to arrange footwear neatly (in an entryway, etc.)

sentences.japanese: 履き物を着用する
sentences.english: to wear footwear

sentences.japanese: 履き物を履き替える
sentences.english: to change footwear

sentences.japanese: 履き物を選ぶ
sentences.english: to choose footwear

sentences.japanese: ワニカニでレベルアップした日の履き物は、いつもより少し軽く感じる。
sentences.english: My shoes always feel a little lighter on WaniKani level-up days.

sentences.japanese: アマゾンから、注文より二足余計に履き物が送られてきました。
sentences.english: Amazon sent me two more pairs of shoes than I ordered.

sentences.japanese: 「ここで履き物を脱いでください」と「ここでは着物を脱いでください」を平仮名で書くと全く同じになる。
sentences.english: When you write "Please take shoes off here" and "Please take kimonos off here" in hiragana, they look exactly the same.

sentences.japanese: 日本語で、屋内の履き物は「上履き」、屋外の履き物は「外履き」と呼ばれます。
sentences.english: In Japanese, indoor footwear is called "uwabaki" and outdoor footwear is called "sotobaki."

meaningMnemonic: You've learned 英 means "England," but it can also mean excel . So what kind of person excels at being brave ? A hero ! 英雄 is a relatively formal word often used to describe historical or legendary heroes, like William Wallace or King Arthur. In more casual contexts, like when talking about superheroes or referring to your dad as your hero, ヒーロー is more common.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 彼の行動はまさに英雄的だった。
sentences.english: His actions were truly heroic.

sentences.japanese: あいつは運だけで実力もないくせに英雄気取りで本当にムカつく。
sentences.english: I’m pissed off at that guy who only has luck and no real ability, but pretends as if he were a hero.

sentences.japanese: あのサッカー選手、あの試合の最後のゴールで一気に英雄あつかいされるようになったね。
sentences.english: That soccer player instantly started being treated like a hero after scoring that last goal in the game, huh?

meaningMnemonic: Remember how you learned that 迷う means "to go astray" or "to get lost?" Well, when you feel like you've gone astray or gotten lost, you might act with hesitation and indecision . You suddenly have doubt about where to go or what to do next. While 迷う can mean getting lost either physically or mentally, 迷い most often conveys an abstract sense of inner conflict or uncertainty, especially in decision making.
readingMnemonic: You learned this reading already when you learned 迷う ! Just swap the う for an い .

sentences.japanese: 迷いがあるなら、もう少し考えたほうがいいよ。
sentences.english: If you have doubts, you should think it over a bit more.

sentences.japanese: 彼の言葉には、少し迷いが感じられました。
sentences.english: I sensed some hesitation in his words.

sentences.japanese: なんとか迷いを断ち切りました。
sentences.english: I managed to get rid of my hesitation.

sentences.japanese: 会社を辞めることに迷いはありませんでした。
sentences.english: I had no hesitation about quitting the company.

sentences.japanese: 彼女は迷いなく、プロジェクトを引き受けた。
sentences.english: She accepted the project without any hesitation.

meaningMnemonic: The master sponsor for an event is the host who's hosting (and possibly sponsoring) it. 主催 is a formal term often used in business, official events, or public gatherings. While it can imply sponsorship, it mainly refers to the act of leading and organizing an event or activity, as well as the person or group hosting it.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 芸能人主催のゴルフ大会ってどんなのなんだろう？
sentences.english: I wonder what a golf tournament hosted by a celebrity is like.

sentences.japanese: このイベントは、地元の商工会が主催しています。
sentences.english: This event is hosted by the local chamber of commerce.

sentences.japanese: 実はこのコンサートの主催は、とある有名な音楽プロデューサーなんです。
sentences.english: Actually, the host of this concert is a well-known music producer.

sentences.japanese: 競馬場の芝についてのシンポジウムが市当局の主催で開かれた。
sentences.english: The racetrack turf symposium was able to happen because of city government sponsorship.

meaningMnemonic: Your house politics are in the hands of one lady : your housekeeper . Your housekeeper knows more about your house than you do — she cleans the place, after all — so it's only natural that she would control all its politics too. Note that it's common to use the polite honorific さん when talking about a 家政婦さん !
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 分別のある家政婦さんで良かったよ。
sentences.english: I'm glad that she is a sensible maid.

sentences.japanese: いくつか個人面接をしてこの家政婦さんに決めました。
sentences.english: After conducting several individual interviews, I decided on this housekeeper.

sentences.japanese: 私はナニーなんで、家政婦とは違います。
sentences.english: I am a nanny, not a housekeeper.

sentences.japanese: 家政婦さんに来てもらおうかと思っているんです。
sentences.english: I'm thinking of having a housekeeper come.

meaningMnemonic: A master lady is a lady who's in charge of a house. In other words, she's a housewife or a homemaker ! In Japan, this is a pretty common profession for married ladies, although things have been changing little by little. Still, being a housewife means you control the money, which is pretty neat if you ask me.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: その主婦は、株で三万円もうけた。
sentences.english: The housewife made 30,000 yen from stocks.

sentences.japanese: 浜田さんはカリスマ主婦のブログを一日三回はチェックしている。
sentences.english: Hamada-san checks a blog written by a charismatic housewife at least three times a day.

sentences.japanese: あの主婦は料理がすごく上手で、今では近所にレストランを開いています。
sentences.english: That housewife is very good at cooking, and now runs a restaurant in the neighborhood.

sentences.japanese: ボタンひとつでご飯とおかずが完成するお手軽さは、忙しい主婦にとってかなり有難いのである。
sentences.english: The ease with which rice and side dishes can be prepared at the touch of a button is quite appreciated by busy housewives.

meaningMnemonic: When your belly has decreased in the amount of stuff inside it, you become hungry . 腹が減った is a casual way of saying I'm hungry in Japanese, often with a bit of a rough or masculine tone.
readingMnemonic: The reading is 腹 plus 減る put together. With these two combined, you have はらがへった . In casual speech, you might hear 腹減った without the が more often. The version with が is more common in writing or fixed expressions like 腹が減っては戦ができぬ (you can't fight on an empty stomach).

sentences.japanese: 腹が減ったなぁ。何か作ってよ。
sentences.english: I'm hungry. Can you make something for me?

sentences.japanese: 腹が減ったよ〜！でもお弁当もう全部食べちゃった。
sentences.english: I'm starving! But I already ate my bento.

sentences.japanese: さっき食べたばっかなのに、もう腹が減ったの？
sentences.english: You just ate a little while ago, and you're already hungry again?

sentences.japanese: 腹が減ったな。この件については、昼飯を食べながら話さないか？
sentences.english: I’m hungry. Would you like to continue this over lunch?

meaningMnemonic: You search then pull items from the index — you know, that list of keywords in alphabetical order at the end of a nonfiction book. Or in 五十音順 order, if you're fancy enough to be reading Japanese!
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just think of the first part of the word in dex ( いん ). Where do you search? In the index.

sentences.japanese: 索引の見方が分かりません。
sentences.english: I don't know how to look at the index.

sentences.japanese: 索引を引いた方が速いんじゃない？
sentences.english: Wouldn't it be faster to look it up in the index?

sentences.japanese: 索引にはすべての用語がアルファベット順に並んでいます。
sentences.english: All of the terms in the index are listed in alphabetical order.

sentences.japanese: 英語索引も付けた方がいいんじゃないかな。
sentences.english: We should make an English index too.

meaningMnemonic: When you enter an inlet , you've gone into the inlet . It's also where water goes inside of the inlet (it's entering the inlet from the ocean, or whatever), so that's another way to think about it.
readingMnemonic: For this reading, just imagine this as 入り with 江 pushed on at the end! Also note this is commonly written as 入江 , but the reading stays the same!

sentences.japanese: 静かな入り江で泳ぎました。
sentences.english: We swam in a quiet cove.

sentences.japanese: この入り江にはイルカがよくあそびに来ると入江さんが言っていた。
sentences.english: Mr. Irie told me that dolphins often visit this cove.

sentences.japanese: バルト海の北の入り江で知らない人からプロポーズされたんですが、とてもロマンチックだったのでつい承諾してしまったんです。
sentences.english: I was proposed to by someone I didn’t know in a cove north of the Baltic Sea. It was so romantic that I couldn't help accepting.

meaningMnemonic: The 日 refers to "Japan" (It's the 日 of 日本 ). So, you have Japan and Europe , which makes this Japan and Europe or Japanese-European . 日欧 is a fairly formal word commonly found in newspapers or official reports, where it’s often used for brevity when referring to Japan and Europe together, like in 日欧関係 (Japanese-European relations).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 水野さんは仕事で日欧を行き来することが多い。
sentences.english: Mizuno-san goes back and forth from Japan to Europe a lot for her work.

sentences.japanese: 日欧間の時差があるので、会議の時間を調整するのが大変です。
sentences.english: Since there's a time difference between Japan and Europe, it's hard to coordinate meetings.

sentences.japanese: 来月、日欧文化交流フェスティバルが開催されます。
sentences.english: The Japan-Europe cultural exchange festival will be held next month.

sentences.japanese: 日欧貿易に関する会議は、司会者の不在によって横道に逸れてしまった。
sentences.english: The meeting concerning trade between Europe and Japan was sidetracked due to the moderator’s absence.

meaningMnemonic: Take the 日 from 日本 (Japan) and the 韓 from 韓国 (Korea), and stick 'em together to get an abbreviation for Japan and South Korea . 日韓 is a bit formal, so you'll usually see it in newspapers or reports referring to Japan and South Korea together. Think international relations and soccer matches.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: この風習は日韓両国でよく見られます。
sentences.english: This custom is frequently seen in both Japan and Korea.

sentences.japanese: 日韓の歴史について学ぶことは、とても重要です。
sentences.english: Learning about the history between Japan and Korea is very important.

sentences.japanese: 日韓のサッカー試合はいつも熱い戦いになります。
sentences.english: Japan-Korea soccer matches always turn into intense battles.

sentences.japanese: 1965年に日韓基本条約が締結されました。
sentences.english: In 1965, The Japan-Republic of Korea Basic Relations Treaty became in effect.

meaningMnemonic: You dry out your cup of liquid after saying Kanpai , or cheers ! 乾杯 means toast ing with your drink and is how you say "Cheers!" in Japanese. It literally means "dry your cup" (drink up), so traditionally, people would finish their drink after saying it. But it's much more relaxed nowadays—most people just take a sip for 乾杯 .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just watch out for the はい turning into ぱい !

sentences.japanese: みんなで乾杯しましょう！
sentences.english: Let's all toast together!

sentences.japanese: 三年ぶりの再会に、乾杯！
sentences.english: Cheers to our first reunion after three years!

sentences.japanese: 少しおくれるので、先に乾杯して始めてください。
sentences.english: I'll be a bit late, so please kanpai without me and start the party.

sentences.japanese: さあ、乾杯、乾杯！それ、ぐいと一杯、飲み干したまえ。
sentences.english: Alright, cheers cheers! Hey, bottoms up!

meaningMnemonic: You examine then search . These are the steps you take in order to perform a lookup of some kind. Or, as the case may be in modern times, do an internet search . 検索 originally referred to looking up information in books or using indexes and reference cards, like in a library. These days it's almost always used for digital and online searches.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 後でネットで検索してみるよ。
sentences.english: I'll look it up on the Internet later.

sentences.japanese: 私がよく利用する検索エンジンはグーグルです。
sentences.english: The search engine I use most often is Google.

sentences.japanese: この本には検索しやすいように索引がついている。
sentences.english: This book has an index for easy reference.

sentences.japanese: こんなにたくさんの料理本を持っているのに、結局クックパッドで検索しちゃうんですよね。
sentences.english: I have so many cookbooks, but I end up searching on Cookpad.

meaningMnemonic: I will diagnose you by making an informed guess during this medical exam . 診察 is what a doctor does when they take a look at you — a medical examination or medical consultation . Keep in mind this doesn't refer to specific medical tests you might undergo to help the doctor diagnose you. (For those, you'd use 検査 .)
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 今日は病院で診察を受けます。
sentences.english: I'm going to have a medical examination at the hospital today.

sentences.japanese: 診察中に、医者に色々と質問しました。
sentences.english: I asked the doctor various questions during the examination.

sentences.japanese: 診察代、いくらぐらいになるかな？
sentences.english: I wonder how much the doctor's visit will cost.

sentences.japanese: 先生は診察の予定がみっちり詰まっています。
sentences.english: The doctor has a jam-packed medical exam schedule.

meaningMnemonic: A big servant is a really important servant — you know, one who serves a king or some other political leader. What do we call a big, highfalutin servant who prances around doing jobs for the leader? A minister . 大臣 refers to high-ranking government officials who oversee ministries or departments, and it can be translated in different ways depending on the country and its political system, such as cabinet minister , state minister , or secretary of state .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 大臣の発言がニュースで大きく取り上げられました。
sentences.english: The minister's statement was widely covered in the news.

sentences.japanese: 財務大臣が来年度の予算案を発表しました。
sentences.english: The Finance Minister announced next year's budget plan.

sentences.japanese: お言葉ですが、大臣は、国民の声をもっとしっかりと聞くべきだと思います。
sentences.english: With all due respect, Minister, I believe you should listen more carefully to the voices of the people.

sentences.japanese: 彼女は大臣たちに会議の前に資料を配るのを忘れてしまったために、首になっちゃったんだよ。
sentences.english: She was fired because she forgot to hand out the documents to the cabinet members before the meeting.

meaningMnemonic: The navigation method s are the methods used for navigation . 航法 is a technical term for navigation, specifically referring to the techniques and methods used to guide a ship, aircraft, or spacecraft from one place to another.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: どこで空中航法を学んだんですか。
sentences.english: Where did you learn aerial navigation?

sentences.japanese: 私のおばあちゃんは、飛行船の航法計算ができるんです。
sentences.english: My grandmother can do navigational calculations for airships.

sentences.japanese: この機体の後ろのところに航法士が乗ってナビしてたんだって。
sentences.english: I heard that the navigator used to sit in the back of this aircraft to navigate.

sentences.japanese: 天則航法を学んでおいたおかげで迷わずに港に着くことができました。
sentences.english: Thanks to my knowledge of celestial navigation, I was able to arrive at the port without getting lost.

meaningMnemonic: Your tense body begins to stretch tighter and tighter as nervousness takes over. 緊張 describes that nervousness you feel before a big event or during a stressful moment. It can also refer to other things that feel tight or strained, like muscle tension , or even global tensions and strained relations between countries.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 社長のジョークに緊張の糸がほぐれました。
sentences.english: The president's joke helped ease the tension.

sentences.japanese: 面接のときは、緊張で手汗が止まりませんでした。
sentences.english: My hands wouldn't stop sweating from nervousness during the interview.

sentences.japanese: 緊張感がただよう会場の中、彼女は静かに立ち上がった。
sentences.english: Amidst the palpable tension in the room, she quietly stood up.

sentences.japanese: 「明日、就職の面接があるんで、ちょっと緊張してるんだよね。」「え〜そうなの？うまくいくといいね。」
sentences.english: "I have a job interview tomorrow. I'm a little nervous." "Oh, really? Well, I'm sure you'll do fine."

sentences.japanese: 仕事から来るストレスと緊張で、最近よく眠れないんです。
sentences.english: I've been having trouble sleeping lately due to stress and tension from work.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 直行 is "nonstop"? Well, with 直航 it's the same thing, but it's only used for flights and boat trips, making this a nonstop flight or direct voyage .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: この船は神戸港に直航します。
sentences.english: This ship is on a direct voyage to Kobe Port.

sentences.japanese: 子供がまだ小さいのでできれば直航の飛行機で行きたいと思っています。
sentences.english: My children are still small, so I would like to take a direct flight if possible.

sentences.japanese: この便はポートランドから東京まで直航せず、途中でアラスカに寄港します。
sentences.english: This flight doesn't go directly from Portland to Tokyo; it makes a stop in Alaska along the way.

meaningMnemonic: When you sponsor an announce ment, you're allowing those you're sponsoring to create some kind of notice for all those they want to get in contact with. 催告 refers to the act of officially notifying someone with a formal notice , urging them to take action within a specified time frame. It's a technical term mainly used in legal or business contexts, like reminding someone to fulfill obligations such as payments or contracts.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: ついに、最終催告を送り付けられてしまいました。
sentences.english: I've finally received the final notification.

sentences.japanese: 催告に応じることが出来ず、クレジットカードが止められてしまった。
sentences.english: Since I could not respond to the payment notification, my credit card got suspended.

sentences.japanese: 住宅ローンが払えなかったため、催告書がきてしまいました。
sentences.english: I received a demand notice because I couldn't pay the mortgage.

sentences.japanese: サラ金から、借金の返済を求める催告状が何度も何度も届いています。
sentences.english: A consumer credit company has been sending me notification letters over and over, demanding that I pay back my debt.

meaningMnemonic: Odd numbers are odd numbers (as in, 1, 3, 5, 7, though they are a bit strange as well).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 奇数を3才の子どもに説明するのは難しいです。
sentences.english: It's difficult to explain odd numbers to a three-year-old.

sentences.japanese: 何故か奇数の月はイベントが多い気がします。
sentences.english: For some reason, I feel like there are more events in odd-numbered months.

sentences.japanese: 参加者の数が奇数だから、ペアになってもらうには一人足りないね。
sentences.english: Because the number of participants is odd, we're one person short for pairing everyone up.

sentences.japanese: 奇数とは2で割り切れない数字のことです。
sentences.english: Odd numbers are numbers that cannot be divided by two.

meaningMnemonic: Conserve those letters with abbreviation and now you're omitting all the extra fluff! 省略 is a relatively formal word used when you are intentionally leaving out something for the sake of brevity or simplicity, like an unneeded explanation or a long-winded greeting. It can also sometimes refer to the abbreviation of a word or phrase.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 日本語の会話では、必要なとき以外は文法上の主語を省略するのがデフォルトです。
sentences.english: In Japanese conversation, it is the default to omit grammatical subjects except when necessary.

sentences.japanese: ここは大切なポイントだから省略しないで全部書くように。
sentences.english: This is an important point, so don't omit anything and write everything down.

sentences.japanese: 賞味期限の所に「Ma」って書いてあるんだけど、「March」の省略かな、それとも「May」の省略かな？
sentences.english: It says "Ma" at the expiry date, but I wonder if this is an abbreviation of "March" or "May".

sentences.japanese: 時間の都合上、今は詳細については省略せざるを得ませんが、また後ほどご説明させて頂きます。
sentences.english: I have to omit the details for now due to time constraints, but I’ll explain it to you later.

meaningMnemonic: One cup of liquid is equal to one cup . It could just be a drink , but if you're measuring exactly one cup, it needs to be full to the brim. That's a lot of liquid—so be careful not to spill! 一杯 mainly refers to the amount that fills a container, like a cup, glass, bowl, or even spoon. It can also describe something being "full," such as a full stomach or a theater at capacity (like how a cup is filled to the brim!). Depending on the context, it can also mean "a lot," as fullness implies abundance. When it uses that meaning, you'll also often see it written in just kana ( いっぱい ).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just remember that 一 becomes いっ , and 杯 becomes ぱい .

sentences.japanese: 「ちょっと一杯飲みに行かない？」「いいね。」
sentences.english: "Let’s go for a drink." "Sounds like a plan."

sentences.japanese: 子供の時に「一杯のかけそば」という映画を一度だけ観たことがあります。
sentences.english: When I was a child, I watched a movie called "One Cup of Soba Noodles in Broth" just once.

sentences.japanese: 次年度の予算のことで頭が一杯な状態だったので、その夜は一杯もお酒を飲む気にはなれなかった。
sentences.english: My mind was so full of the following year's budget that I didn't feel like having even one drink that night.

meaningMnemonic: An "alone" ( 一人 ) daughter is a daughter with no other daughter siblings, making her the only daughter .
readingMnemonic: The readings are 一人 plus 娘 put together into one, single (daughter) word.

sentences.japanese: クララはゼーゼマン家の一人娘です。
sentences.english: Klara is the only daughter of the Sesemann family.

sentences.japanese: 彼には一人娘がいます。
sentences.english: He has an only daughter.

sentences.japanese: 林さんは女手ひとつで一人娘を育てています。
sentences.english: Ms. Hayashi is raising her only daughter by herself.

meaningMnemonic: 痛み is "pain." 止める is "to stop." What stops pain if you use it? How about a painkiller .
readingMnemonic: The reading is 痛み and 止める put together into one word. Not too painful, right? Just remember the rendaku on the ど .

sentences.japanese: 頭痛がひどいので、痛み止めを飲みました。
sentences.english: I had a bad headache, so I took a painkiller.

sentences.japanese: 痛み止めが効いてきて、少し楽になりました。
sentences.english: The painkiller is starting to take effect, and I feel a bit better.

sentences.japanese: 薬局で痛み止めを買ってきてもらえませんか？
sentences.english: Could you pick up some painkillers for me from the pharmacy?

sentences.japanese: 彼は痛み止めを飲んで、また畑を耕し始めた。
sentences.english: He took a painkiller and kept plowing the field.

meaningMnemonic: If you want to ride in a car , the ticket you'll need is a passenger ticket . 乗車券 is primarily a ticket for a train ride, so think of "car" here as a train car. It can also refer to tickets for other rides, like Ferris wheels, cable cars, ropeways, or certain buses that require a prior ticket purchase.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: バスの乗車券はどこで買える？
sentences.english: Where can I buy a bus ticket?

sentences.japanese: 割引乗車券はありますか。
sentences.english: Do you offer discount tickets?

sentences.japanese: 電車の乗車券を内ポケットに入れたはずなのに、見当たらないの。
sentences.english: I was sure I put my train ticket in my inside pocket, but I can't find it.

meaningMnemonic: You learned 恐怖 means "terror," and 〜症 can mean "disease." So what's a terror disease? Well, it's a phobia . In Japanese, 恐怖症 is mostly used as a suffix for specific phobia names, like 高所恐怖症 (acrophobia, or fear of heights). Do you have any 恐怖症 ?
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 私も父も高所恐怖症です。
sentences.english: My dad and I are both afraid of heights.

sentences.japanese: 閉所恐怖症のため、エレベーターに乗るのが苦手です。
sentences.english: I'm claustrophobic, so I have difficulty taking elevators.

sentences.japanese: 上司からパワハラを受けたせいで、対人恐怖症になってしまいました。
sentences.english: Because of the power harassment I experienced from my boss, I've developed social anxiety.

sentences.japanese: ワニカニのやり過ぎで漢字を覚えたのはいいけれど、ワニとカニ恐怖症になってしまった。
sentences.english: I studied kanji on WaniKani too much, and while it was great that I learned kanji, I ended up developing a phobia of alligators and crabs.

meaningMnemonic: Being fierce and angry means you're filled with rage , or for you to be enraged . 激怒 is a relatively formal word, often used in literature to describe someone flying into a rage or experiencing intense, uncontrollable anger. Therefore, you’ll frequently encounter this as a suru-verb in the form of 激怒する .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 大激怒
sentences.english: great fury

sentences.japanese: 激怒をする
sentences.english: to fly into a rage

sentences.japanese: それを見た母は、大激怒でした。
sentences.english: When my mother saw this, she was absolutely furious.

sentences.japanese: 彼は激怒してその場を立ち去りました。
sentences.english: He stormed off in a fit of rage.

sentences.japanese: この映画は、原作を改変しすぎて、ファンを激怒させました。
sentences.english: This movie made significant changes to the original work, which infuriated the fans.

sentences.japanese: 土足でベンチに上がるの、海外ならいいかもしれないけど、日本では激怒ものだよ。
sentences.english: Putting one's shoes on a bench may be fine in other countries, but in Japan it would cause indignation.

meaningMnemonic: Again you build it. This is rebuilding . 再建 is a formal word that refers to the act of rebuilding something that has deteriorated or been lost, whether it's a physical structure like a building or an organization, or a part of the body in the context of medical procedures.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just don't forget that extra い !

sentences.english: to advance reconstruction

sentences.japanese: 再建を目指す
sentences.english: to aim for reconstruction

sentences.english: to carry out reconstruction

sentences.japanese: 再建をする
sentences.english: to reconstruct

sentences.japanese: 再建資金
sentences.english: reconstruction funds

sentences.japanese: 再建手術
sentences.english: reconstruction surgery

sentences.japanese: 再建支援
sentences.english: reconstruction support

sentences.japanese: 再建計画
sentences.english: reconstruction plan

sentences.japanese: 会社再建
sentences.english: rebuilding a company

sentences.japanese: 国家再建
sentences.english: national reconstruction

sentences.japanese: 経営再建
sentences.english: business reconstruction

sentences.japanese: 生活再建
sentences.english: rebuilding one's life

sentences.japanese: 財政再建
sentences.english: financial reconstruction

sentences.japanese: これは国家再建をかけた一大プロジェクトです。
sentences.english: This is a major project aimed at national reconstruction.

sentences.english: To rebuild this building, we will need to secure funding first.

sentences.japanese: 今は被災地の再建が最優先です。
sentences.english: Rebuilding the disaster-stricken areas is top priority now.

sentences.japanese: 経営が苦しくなった会社を再建するまで、彼は毎日規定よりも長い時間働いた。
sentences.english: He worked longer hours than he was supposed to every day until he rebuilt his struggling company.

meaningMnemonic: The religion teach ings are what makes up a religion . If you don't have the teachings of the religion, nobody will learn about it, and it will stop being a religion.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: 彼はさまざまな宗教に関心があります。
sentences.english: He is interested in various religions.

sentences.japanese: 多くの人々にとって、宗教は生活の一部です。
sentences.english: For many people, religion is a part of their daily lives.

sentences.japanese: 時々、ワニカニってカルト宗教みたいだと思うことがあります。
sentences.english: Sometimes, I feel like WaniKani seems a bit like a cult.

sentences.japanese: 彼女が、世界宗教会議の記録を取る書記を務めます。
sentences.english: She will be the secretary who records the transactions of the world religions meeting.

meaningMnemonic: To lend or to rent is 貸す . This is the noun version of that, used as a prefix. It is something that has been rented, a " rental ____," like a 貸しビル (rental office building) or 貸しボート (rental boat).
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as 貸す .

sentences.japanese: これは私のじゃなくて、貸し自転車なんです。
sentences.english: This isn't mine, it's a rental bike.

sentences.japanese: 今は貸し倉庫で寝泊まりしているんです。
sentences.english: I’m living in a rental warehouse now.

sentences.japanese: 今度の休暇は貸し別荘で過ごす予定です。
sentences.english: We are planning to spend the coming holidays at a rental cottage.

meaningMnemonic: You request then you request again… Yep, this sounds like a request to me. 請求 isn't just any old casual request — it's used when formally requesting something from another party. It often involves payment requests (like a charge ), but can also refer to asking for things like application forms or informational materials. It can even refer to the kind of claim you file in court.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how you learned that 怒る means "to get angry?" Well this is when someone else gets angry and it's because YOU made them angry. It means to anger someone . Verbs ending with an あせる sound (like 怒らせる ) often mean that you're causing someone to feel, do, or experience something. So, 怒らせる means you make someone angry. You can remember this because you always make Russell ( らせる ) angry. No matter what you say, you seem to get on his nerves… you're just constantly angering this Russell guy.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned this reading when you learned 怒る , so you should know this one too!

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means ascend so the verb vocab version must be to ascend , or to rise . 昇る is commonly used to talk about things like the sun and the moon rising, or smoke rising from a fire.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the kun'yomi reading, but it's pretty easy. How do you read all the other "to climb" words? 登る is one example. 上る is another. They're all のぼ る , and so is this. Unlike the other climbing words, though, this suggests there's no effort involved. That's why you're "ascending" and not climbing, because climbing is a bit of work.

sentences.english: You'll be alright. The sun will rise again.

meaningMnemonic: You've seen how 捕まえる means "to catch," and this is its intransitive sibling: to be caught . At its core, 捕まる means getting physically caught, whether you've lost a game of tag or been arrested by the police. Sometimes, it can be used in a more figurative sense too, like when you get held up by a really chatty person (you've been "caught" by them) or you finally manage to get a word with someone you've been trying to talk to (they've been "caught" by you). You can tell this apart from 捕まえる by thinking about how it would really mar ( まる ) your reputation if you were to be arrested by the cops.
readingMnemonic: This word uses the same reading as 捕まえる , so if you remember that one, you should be okay here too.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means break and this verb vocab version means to break something . You're the one actively doing the breaking here, so there's always a direct object involved. You know this because someone is trying to sue ( す ) you for the things you've broken.
readingMnemonic: This word uses the kun'yomi reading こわ , which you didn't learn with the kanji. Here's a mnemonic to help you out: When you feel like you want to break something , you go for a koa la ( こわ ). No, not a real koala. A beautiful ceramic koala. Watch it shatter on the ground, because you wanted to go and break it. What a jerk you are.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means draw near , so this verb version is to draw near . It can also mean to stop by , since stopping by a place is like drawing near it briefly, right?
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet so here's a mnemonic to help you: If you're too shy to draw near to people, just learn how to use a yo -yo ( よ )! Then people will draw near to YOU to compliment you on your sick skills. You won't have to do it yourself!

meaningMnemonic: The meaning of this word is the same as 任せる . Both words are pretty common, but 任す is slightly less common than 任せる . Here's the mnemonic again, just in case you need a refresher: If you pass a duty on to someone, that means you're going to entrust something to that person, or you're going to delegate something . In other words, you're going to leave something to them, so that they do it for you.
readingMnemonic: This uses the same reading you learned with 任せる .

meaningMnemonic: What kind of emotion would make your belly 立つ (stand up)? A pretty angry one, I bet. Note that the particle が often drops, especially in casual conversation.

Note that the が isn't always there, though — it's sometimes dropped in casual conversation. meaning: To Get To The Bottom Of

You'll be able to identify something , like the truth. 見極める primarily involves the careful examination and discernment of the underlying aspects or truth of a matter. It emphasizes the thoroughness and effort required to make well-informed decisions or judgments, particularly when the situation is complex or difficult to understand.
readingMnemonic: The readings come from the words 見る and 極める put together. Get to the bottom of this word and learn it.

sentences.japanese: 最近ストレスでよく眠れないんです。
sentences.english: These days, I can't sleep well due to stress.

sentences.japanese: 彼女は電気をつけながら眠るのが好きです。
sentences.english: She likes to sleep with the lights on.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means stuffed , this word means to stuff in , as in you're doing the stuffing. You know this because you're a mail ( める ) carrier, and you always have to stuff mail into people's packed mailboxes. Why don't these people check their mail more? It’s hard work trying to cram in all this junk mail! 詰める refers to tightly fitting something into an available space, like cramming clothes into a suitcase, putting jam into a jar, or even scooting over to make room, as you're squeezing yourself into a narrower space.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned that reading with the kanji, so you should have no troubles here.

sentences.english: I forcefully stuffed a lot of clothes into the suitcase.

sentences.japanese: あんまり詰めすぎると、ファスナーが閉まらなくなるよ。
sentences.english: If you overpack it, the zipper won't close.

sentences.japanese: すいません、もう少し詰めてもらえませんか？
sentences.english: Excuse me, could you move a bit closer together to make some space for me?

sentences.japanese: お弁当にご飯を詰めといてくれない？
sentences.english: Can you put some rice in my bento box for me?

meaningMnemonic: Someone request s something, and you're the one to take on their request. Wow, how nice of you to accept that request! 請ける is a formal word often used in business contexts to describe someone willingly accepting a job, task, or request. For example, you might use 請ける when taking on a new project or accepting customer orders.
readingMnemonic: What's another word for "to accept" or "to receive"? How about 受ける ? They share a reading!

sentences.japanese: この案件を請けるのはリスクが高いですが、チャレンジしてみたいです。
sentences.english: Undertaking this project is risky, but I want to give this challenge a try.

sentences.japanese: 彼女は急な注文でも快く請けてくれることが多いので、本当に助かっています。
sentences.english: She often willingly takes on last-minute requests, which is really helpful.

sentences.japanese: お前の顔を立てるためだけにこのプロジェクトを請けたんだからな。
sentences.english: I only took this project so that you could save face.

sentences.japanese: 仕事を請けるときは、社員が喜んで受ける仕事かを考えて、請けるか決めるんです。売り上げは二の次にしないと、いい仕事はできませんからね。
sentences.english: When taking on a job, I first consider whether it's something the employees will be happy to do. If you don't put profits as a secondary concern, you won't be able to deliver quality work.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means tighten , so the verb vocab version is to tighten .
readingMnemonic: What can you do if you want something to tighten or to become tight ? You need to hug your shee p ( し ) really close until... The sheep tightens into a tiny little ball. Cute!

sentences.japanese: このシートベルトは自動的に締まってくれます。

sentences.english: Mr Onishi's body is well toned isn't it!

sentences.japanese: 初めての管理職ということで、身の引き締まる思いをしています。
sentences.english: This is my first managerial position and I’m very tense.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means urge so the verb vocab version is to urge . 促す means to encourage or to prompt someone to take action or proceed with something. Depending on the context, it can also mean to promote the growth, development, or change of something.
readingMnemonic: Someone with a weird accent is trying to urge you to eat " Unagah " ( うなが ). This person really means "unagi," and this person also doesn't realize how delicious unagi is (and thinks he's tricking you). You ask him what "Unagah" is. Go ahead and say it out loud.

sentences.japanese: 先生は生徒にもっと質問をするよう促した。
sentences.english: The teacher encouraged the students to ask more questions.

sentences.japanese: そのニュースが人々に行動を促すきっかけとなったようです。
sentences.english: It seems that the news prompted people to take action.

sentences.japanese: 医者は禁煙を促されたが、なかなか実行に移せなかった。
sentences.english: The doctor urged me to quit smoking, but I struggled to follow through.

sentences.japanese: このキャンペーンは、環境に優しい行動を促すことを目的としています。
sentences.english: This campaign aims to promote eco-friendly actions.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means visit and the verb vocab version is also to visit . 訪れる is somewhat formal, so you'll encounter it more in writing than everyday speech. It's used to talk about visiting places, but not people. That's one big difference with the similar-looking 訪ねる . Another is that you don't need a specific purpose for the kind of visiting you do with 訪れる .
readingMnemonic: The reading isn't the same as 訪ねる , though, I'm afraid. It's おとず . Remember how this means just visiting a place? Unfortunately, you completely forgot what you were visiting. When you finally remember, it's because you were looking down to think. It's to look at the toes of the giant Buddha statue. " Oh Toes !" ( おとず ), you exclaim.

sentences.japanese: ここを訪れるのは三年ぶりです。
sentences.english: It has been three years since I have visited here.

sentences.japanese: これは、初めてローマを訪れた時の写真です。
sentences.english: This is a picture of my first visit to Rome.

sentences.japanese: しかし、そんな時に転機が訪れたんです。
sentences.english: But then a turning point came.

sentences.english: If you want to visit the ramen factory you should make your reservations as far in advance as possible.

meaningMnemonic: 研修 is a training or study of some kind. If it's in your current life ( 生 ) that you are doing the training, then you are a trainee . This is a lot like how a student is in the status of "study life."
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. The reading from 研修 should also help you too.

sentences.japanese: 研修生の時期に学んだことが、今の仕事にとても役立っています。
sentences.english: What I learned during my time as a trainee has been very useful in my current job.

sentences.japanese: こちらが、新しい研修生の三浦くんです。
sentences.english: This is the new trainee, Miura.

meaningMnemonic: Two cups of liquid is equals to two cups or two drinks . The contents don't have to be liquid — you can use 二杯 for two bowls of rice or two spoons of sugar as well.

readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: To calm my mind, I went to a Zen temple and tried Zen meditation.

sentences.japanese: 禅宗の教えに従って、彼はシンプルな生活を心がけています。
